findings.headline: Axios: Treasury turning to 'verbal intervention' to steady bond market — Bessent doubling down on buybacks
findings.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent is using buyback operations and public signaling as 'effectively the equivalent of verbal intervention from the U.S.' to suppress long-end yields. Elevated rates keeping mortgages and loans painfully expensive alongside inflationary fallout from Iran war. This is an unprecedented Treasury intervention posture.

findings.headline: Japan MoF officials repeatedly warning of 'excessive' yen moves, standing ready to act
findings.summary: Finance Minister Katayama and other officials issuing repeated verbal intervention warnings. Yen at ~159 after failed joint US-Japan intervention. Carry trade dynamics reinforced by rising US yields. Japanese investors sold $29.6B of US debt in Q1 2026 alone.

findings.headline: Cambridge Currencies: No major central bank cutting, three with hawkish dissenters — unusual market structure
findings.summary: The defining feature of current FX market is that no major central bank is cutting rates and three have hawkish dissenters. This is unusual and changes the currency risk profile — simultaneous hawkish posture from Fed, ECB, and BoJ creates a race-to-tighten dynamic.

findings.headline: 150+ anonymous Polymarket wallets used non-public US military info to bet on operations — 97.2% win rate
findings.summary: More than 150 anonymous wallets on Polymarket may have used non-public information about US military operations to place bets, collectively earning ~$8M with average win probability of 97.2%. This signals insider knowledge of military actions leaking to prediction markets — a new form of information leakage.

findings.headline: Leaked Basij militia recording: Iranian internal anxiety about new protests and member identification risk
findings.summary: Leaked recording of Iran's Basij militia officials weighing risk of new protests and danger of members being identified online. Rare glimpse of anxiety inside the force used to suppress demonstrators. Suggests regime internal cohesion is weakening under economic pressure.

findings.headline: Truth Social sale of fast access to Trump posts draws securities law concerns
findings.summary: Lawsuit alleges Truth Social product selling fast access to Trump posts is unconstitutional; experts warn it could violate securities laws. Highlights regulatory risk around political-financial information asymmetry.

findings.headline: BoJ entered 'new phase requiring flexibility' — summary of opinions shows shift toward nimble risk-aware policy
findings.summary: BoJ summary underscored a new phase requiring flexibility rather than preset path. Concerns over weak growth eased but inflationary pressures may strengthen. Policymakers emphasized clearly signaling determination to prevent excessive price gains. Shift toward more nimble, risk-aware management.

findings.headline: ECB cut rates 8 times Jun 2024-Jun 2025, then held unchanged — pause extending into Q3 2026
findings.source: UK House of Commons Library / ECB
findings.summary: ECB cut rates eight times from June 2024 to June 2025, before leaving rates unchanged until June 2026 and beyond. The pause is now extending despite economic weakness, suggesting ECB sees persistent inflation risks. This creates a stagflationary signal for the Eurozone.

findings.headline: Fed FOMC July 28-29 minutes released Aug 19 — Governor Cook speech on US and Alaskan economies Aug 5
findings.summary: FOMC July minutes released. No rate cut signaled despite bond market pressure. Treasury Secretary at odds with Fed, using buybacks to contain long-end yields without Fed cooperation. Fed-Treasury tension is itself a systemic risk signal.

findings.headline: PM Takaichi signals acceptance of BoJ rate hike as soon as September 16 — striking reversal
findings.summary: PM Takaichi signaled she'd accept a BoJ rate hike as soon as September 16, a striking reversal from last October when she called the idea 'stupid.' Her party has come around to the view that weak yen is importing inflation too fast. BoJ research team cut GDP forecast to 0.9% from 1.3% while inflation forecast at 2.2%.

findings.headline: US imposes new sanctions on Hezbollah, threatens economic pressure on Iran — oil rises to $94
findings.summary: US imposes new sanctions on Hezbollah and threatens further economic pressure on Iran. Global crude rose to nearly $94/barrel — highest since late July. VP Vance says economic pressure remains 'most effective tool.' Iran has developed 'survival economy' sustaining pain over time. Secondary sanctions on China could trigger all-out trade war.

findings.headline: Trump's new Iran sanctions could trigger trade war with China — and backfire on the dollar
findings.summary: If US opts for tough secondary sanctions against China over Iran trade, an all-out trade war could shatter the global market. Geopolitical analyst Brandon Weichert warns of all-out trade war scenario. This directly links the Iran war to the China trade war thread.

findings.headline: Israel moves against Turkiye — risk of broader regional conflagration escalating
findings.summary: Israel-Turkiye tensions rising as Israel 'moves against Turkiye,' risking broader conflagration beyond the Iran conflict. This adds a second Middle East flashpoint. Bessent at odds with Fed in move to contain longer-dated Treasury yields — Treasury-Fed conflict is itself a geopolitical risk.

findings.headline: Iranian Supreme Leader appointed hardliners to 7 top military/security positions — institutionalizing offensive shift
findings.summary: Mojtaba Khamenei appointed hardliners to seven top positions in Iranian military and security apparatus on August 10, 2026. This institutionalizes an offensive shift in Iranian foreign policy and prepares the regime for escalation rather than negotiation.

findings.headline: Strait of Hormuz traffic at trickle — oil markets pricing in prolonged crisis, Brent at $94
findings.summary: Iran war has disrupted global travel and trade, halted Middle East flights, and led to shipping reroutes to avoid Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea. Oil market pricing in prolonged Hormuz crisis. Brent crude at ~$94/barrel, highest since late July. US gas prices at highest ever recorded for August. Ship-to-ship transfers and leaky blockade partially alleviating but not resolving.

findings.headline: Memory chip shortage persists through 2026 — SK Hynix warns may last past 2030, TSMC CoWoS fully booked
findings.summary: Memory chip shortage driven by AI capacity reallocation creating scarcity for consumer/enterprise markets. TSMC's CoWoS capacity substantially booked through 2026. New fab capacity from Micron and SK Hynix not expected before 2027. AI disruption forcing $100B inflection in advanced chip packaging. Geopolitical dimension with US export controls on China.

findings.headline: Red Sea shipping disruption and Strait of Hormuz tensions creating compound supply chain risk
findings.summary: Multiple simultaneous supply chain chokepoints: Red Sea shipping disruption affecting Asia-Europe corridor, Strait of Hormuz tensions around energy route, and evolving semiconductor export controls. Vendors depending on same semiconductor fab or logistics hub means disruption affects all supposed alternatives at once.

findings.headline: August 2026 transport report: Middle East conditions continue to affect airline networks and capacity
findings.summary: Technology and high-value time-sensitive shipments influencing cargo flows in Asia. Evolving Middle East conditions affecting airline networks and capacity. Fuel costs and geopolitical uncertainty adding pressure. Shippers need to monitor individual trade lanes.

findings.headline: SEC proposes new 'Regulation Crypto Assets' — first formal US crypto regulatory framework
findings.summary: SEC proposed Regulation Crypto Assets (Reg CA) on August 18, 2026, creating a dedicated offering framework for crypto assets. Two exemptions for crypto-related offerings with targeted disclosure and reporting regimes. This is the first formal US regulatory regime for digital token sales under federal securities laws. Could reshape crypto market structure.

findings.headline: CLARITY Act: Senate filed cloture Aug 8, no final floor vote — passage likely slips to 2027
findings.summary: Senate filed cloture motion August 8 for CLARITY Act but still no final floor vote. Missed August 10 recess deadline means passage likely slips to 2027. Legislative uncertainty for crypto regulation persists. Combined with SEC's Reg CA proposal, creates a bifurcated regulatory signal.

findings.headline: US secondary sanctions on China over Iran trade — regulatory trigger for trade war escalation
findings.summary: New economic measures paired with continued restrictions on Iranian maritime trade and port access. Renewed sanctions and enforcement campaign launched July 2026 after Trump resumed military operations against Iran and reinstated Strait of Hormuz blockade. Secondary sanctions on any global entity trading in dollars with Iran — directly threatens China.

findings.headline: 2025-2026 Iranian protests ongoing — nationwide demonstrations amid deepening economic crisis
findings.summary: Series of nationwide demonstrations against Iranian government that began December 28, 2025 amid deepening economic crisis. Unrest followed sharp depreciation of Iranian rial, rising inflation, and widespread shortages. Basij militia leaked recording shows internal anxiety about new protest round. Regime hardliner appointments suggest preparation for crackdown rather than concession.

findings.headline: Tunisians protest against President Saied — growing political and economic crisis in North Africa
findings.summary: Activists and opponents of Tunisian President Kais Saied took to streets of Tunis calling for his departure and restoration of democracy. Latest protest amid growing political and economic crisis. Adds to Mediterranean rim instability alongside Iran war fallout.

findings.headline: Syrians march in Aleppo over death of man allegedly beaten by security forces
findings.summary: Syrians marched in Aleppo over death of Mohammad Ghamira, 29, father of two and former White Helmets volunteer, arrested and allegedly beaten by security forces. Civil unrest in post-Assad Syria adds another Middle East instability vector.

findings.headline: Gen Z protests across Asia — India NEET exam protests, broader anti-elite capture movement
findings.summary: Gen Z protests across Asia linked to long-standing elite capture and insufficient inclusive development. India youth protests focused on NEET-UG exam paper leak. Broader challenge to 'business as usual' politics. Underlying social pressure in Asian economies adds instability vector.

findings.headline: Global bond markets on fire — 10-year Treasury at 4.683% (highest since 2007), 30-year at 5.216% (highest since 2001)
findings.summary: Treasury 10-year yield at 4.683% — highest since eve of 2007 global financial crisis. 30-year at 5.216% — highest since 2001. Global bond selloff led by Japan. Three separate US economic releases pointed toward lower yields yet long-end rose anyway — pressure overrides data. Brookings: 'reckless fiscal policy catching up with governments.' Barclays: investors combing debt markets for cracks, wary of SVB-repeat.

findings.headline: Yen carry trade described as 'giant Jenga tower' — $1T+ in Treasuries at risk if Japan unwinds
findings.summary: Ed Yardeni: 'Financial system looks like a giant Jenga tower with the yen as a load-bearing piece.' Japan is largest foreign holder of US debt at $1T+. Japanese investors sold $29.6B of US debt in Q1 2026. Once rapid yen appreciation triggers forced deleveraging, what is sold won't be just US Treasuries but the most liquid, highly-valued technology stock positions. Carry trade is one of the most crowded trades in global markets and most prone to violent unwinding.

findings.headline: Goldman Sachs: Consumer spending growth to slow to 1% in H2 2026 — slowest since pandemic recovery
findings.summary: Goldman Sachs warns real consumer spending growth could slow to as low as 1% in H2 2026, down from 2.5% annual growth in June. Retail sales dropped 0.6% in July. Fading tax refund tailwinds and higher energy prices (Brent at $89, +22% pre-Iran war) driving the slowdown. This would be the slowest pace of spending since early 2021.

findings.headline: Crypto flash crash: $108B wiped out, $1.7B liquidated in 24 hours — Bitcoin tests $80K, ETH at $1,874
findings.source: Coinpedia / Yahoo Finance / CoinDesk / Bitcoin Foundation
findings.summary: Crypto flash crash wiped out $108B market cap with $1.7B in liquidations in 24 hours. Bitcoin down 29% YoY, facing $80K test. Ethereum down 59.6% YoY at $1,874. XRP fell 37% in one day. Total crypto cap at $2.1T, down 52% from October 2025 peak. Analysts questioning timing of bear market bottom. Two conditions need to flip before recovery can start.

findings.headline: China property crisis: 5-year downward spiral continues — Shanghai rolls out new easing as economy slows
findings.source: Bloomberg / AP / Foreign Affairs / People News Today
findings.summary: China's property market in downward spiral for 5 years. Real estate values continue to plummet, households in financial distress forced to sell. Evergrande founder gets life sentence, cleanup ongoing after $300B default. Shanghai rolled out fresh easing measures — first top-tier city to support residential market after economic slowdown deepened in July. Foreign Affairs: provincial revenues could collapse with tumble in land sales, unemployment in coastal manufacturing provinces could turn them against Beijing. China's $1.2T trade surplus at breaking point — global appetite for Chinese overcapacity is finite and shrinking.

findings.headline: Naked Capitalism: Bessent at odds with Fed — Treasury intervening in long end without Fed cooperation
findings.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent intervening in long end of Treasury market, putting him at odds with the Federal Reserve. This is an unprecedented Treasury-Fed conflict. The more likely bad outcomes than overhyped dollar crash are either a financial market meltdown (AI debt and equity bubbles as detonators) or Japanification — managing to avoid overt debt writedowns at cost of economic strangulation. Too much private debt relative to GDP in many economies means contagion into other debt types is likely.

japan_yen.assessment: Japan yen is the single most dangerous thread in the global financial system. Three independent lead indicator categories converge: verbal intervention from US and Japan, BoJ communication signaling September rate hike, and financial stress precursors showing JGB yields at 29-year highs, carry trade described as 'giant Jenga tower.' PM Takaichi's reversal on rate hike acceptance is a regime change signal. $1T+ in Treasuries at risk if carry trade unwinds.

us_recession.assessment: US recession risk is the highest convergence score recorded. Six of eight lead indicator categories point at this thread. Treasury yields at 2007/2001 levels, Goldman warning consumer spending to slow to 1%, Treasury-Fed conflict, Iran war driving oil to $94, secondary sanctions threatening China trade war, and Japan carry trade at risk of unwinding. This is a multi-vector crisis converging on the US economy.

middle_east_war.assessment: Middle East war is ACTIVE and escalating. Five lead indicator categories converge. New US sanctions on Hezbollah, Israel-Turkiye tensions adding second flashpoint, Hormuz traffic at trickle, oil at $94, Iranian internal anxiety (leaked Basij recording), hardliner appointments institutionalizing offensive shift, and ongoing Iranian protests. This is no longer a developing signal — it is an active, multi-front crisis.

china_collapse.assessment: China collapse risk is now ACTIVE. Five categories converge. Property crisis in 5-year downward spiral, Evergrande cleanup after $300B default, Shanghai easing measures signal desperation. Foreign Affairs warns provincial revenues could collapse. US secondary sanctions over Iran trade threaten to trigger all-out trade war. Gen Z protests in Asia add social pressure. China's $1.2T trade surplus at breaking point as global appetite for overcapacity shrinks.

euro_crisis.assessment: Euro crisis is DEVELOPING. Five categories converge but with lower intensity. ECB paused rates despite weakness (stagflation signal), Red Sea disruption affecting Asia-Europe corridor, global bond selloff spreading to Eurozone, Tunisian instability on Mediterranean rim. Europe's de-industrialization from lost Russian energy compounds vulnerability. Not yet at active crisis but trajectory is negative.

asian_contagion.assessment: Asian contagion is DEVELOPING. BoJ rate hike signal from Takaichi could trigger carry trade unwinding across Asia. China property crisis and economic slowdown spilling over. Gen Z protests add social dimension. Asian economies in better shape than 1998 crisis but yen carry trade unwinding would hit all of them simultaneously.

crypto_collapse.assessment: Crypto collapse is DEVELOPING but already partially materialized. Crypto cap down 52% from October 2025 peak. $108B flash crash on Aug 22. Bitcoin at $80K test, ETH at $1,874. SEC Reg CA proposal and CLARITY Act delay create regulatory uncertainty. Yen carry trade unwinding would compound crypto sell-off as leveraged positions are forced to deleverage. If Japan hikes rates September 16, crypto could face another liquidation cascade.

global_pandemic.assessment: No lead indicators detected for pandemic risk in this scan cycle.
